candidate.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance: provide education and care for prevention and early detection of health problems; identify risk factors and recommended screening based on client needs.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — CKD risk recognition and early screening
candidate.educational_objective: Teach clients with CKD risk factors that early disease can be asymptomatic and that screening includes assessment of both eGFR and urine albumin.

options.A: Kidney screening can wait until swelling or urine changes develop.
options.B: A normal urine appearance rules out early chronic kidney disease.
options.C: Only a serum creatinine level is needed to screen for chronic kidney disease.
options.D: Early kidney disease may have no symptoms, so at-risk clients are screened with kidney-function and urine-albumin testing.

candidate.rationale: NIDDK identifies diabetes and hypertension as major CKD risk factors and notes that early kidney disease may have no symptoms; testing may be the only way to detect it. NIDDK recommends screening people at risk using urine albumin assessment and estimated GFR from serum creatinine. Therefore D is correct. A delays detection until symptomatic disease, B incorrectly relies on urine appearance, and C omits urine albumin, one of the two key CKD markers.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Diabetes and hypertension increase CKD risk; early CKD may be asymptomatic, and at-risk screening uses both urine albumin and eGFR assessment.
candidate.source_document_title: Identify & Evaluate Patients with Chronic Kidney Disease; Preventing Chronic Kidney Disease
candidate.source_locator: Identify & Evaluate Patients with CKD > Identify Patients with CKD: screen people at risk including diabetes and hypertension; two key markers are urine albumin and eGFR. Preventing CKD: early kidney disease may have no symptoms, so getting tested may be the only way to know kidney health; manage conditions such as diabetes and high blood pressure.
candidate.source_organization: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK), NIH
candidate.stem: A client with diabetes and hypertension says, 'My kidneys must be fine because I don't have any urinary symptoms.' Which response by the nurse is best?
